role: The code map's call graph: parses every Swift file with tree-sitter for calls, property reads, bare references, conformances and closure assignments; resolves each to unit keys as certain or possible edges; adds recorded calls, protocol-requirement dispatch and Makefile/workflow/script wiring. `build` is the from-scratch definition; index.py keeps the same graph up to date incrementally from the same parts (unit_table, recorded_edges, swift_file, Resolver, wiring_edges, assemble). Imported by index.py and codemap.py.
state: COMMON: member names (count, map, load, save, start, reset, ...) so common in Swift/Foundation/SwiftUI that a unique repo match on an unknown receiver is only a possible edge
NOT_A_REFERENCE: syntax-node parent types under which a simple_identifier is a declaration, label, type or member name rather than a reference
RANK: edge kinds strongest first (certain 2, implicit 1, possible 0); implicit is a link a framework makes that no call shows

WITNESS: member names the frameworks call on a type's behalf (SwiftUI body, makeBody, UIKit-wrapper and Layout methods, preference reduce/defaultValue, animatableData, path, makeAsyncIterator, ==, <, hash)
FUNC_KINDS / PROP_KINDS: inventory unit kinds that can be called / read as properties
toplevel: Module docstring defining certain and possible edges, `from __future__ import annotations`, imports (collections, re, Path, NS_CODE from inventory), the constants above, TEST_TARGETS (EmuquTests/, EmuquUITests/), is_test_file, _PARSER (the lazily made Swift parser) and the Resolver class statement. tree_sitter is imported inside swift_file.

units.does: The type names written in a piece of text (words starting with a capital letter), a qualified name such as Outer.Inner taken as its last part.

Parses one Swift file and walks it once, returning five things: refs (unit start line -> list of (kind 'call'|'prop'|'meta', name, argument labels (for 'meta': [the name of the call it is handed to]), trailing-closure count, (receiver kind, receiver type))), params (function/init/subscript start line -> [(external label, has default)]), conforms (type or protocol name -> names in its inheritance clause; extensions included, generic arguments and module prefixes stripped), closure_assigns (stored-property name -> start lines of units that assign a closure literal to it) and contains (type name -> the type names written in its stored properties' type annotations and its enum cases' associated values, each qualified name as its last part). References in code outside every unit (Swift top-level code) are not collected.
Source text of a node: the raw bytes in its byte range, decoded with replacement.
For a call_expression, returns the label of each value argument in its call_suffix ('_' when unlabeled) and the number of trailing closures.

branches.cond: child is not the call suffix

units.does: Classifies what a member reference is made on: no target -> ('implicit', None); self or Self -> ('self', None); super -> ('super', None); a call whose callee is a capitalised identifier (a constructor, `Foo(...)`) -> ('type', 'Foo'); a capitalised dotted name -> ('type', its last component); anything else (a variable, a chain) -> ('unknown', None).

branches.cond: constructor call of a capitalised name

units.does: Recursive walk carrying the start line of the innermost enclosing unit and the name of the innermost enclosing type declaration. A class/struct/enum/extension/protocol declaration adds its inheritance clause to conforms. A function/init/deinit/subscript/protocol-function/property declaration that starts on a unit's start line becomes the current unit; for non-properties its parameters (external name, else name, else '_'; with whether a default follows) go to params. Inside a unit: a call on a bare identifier is an implicit-receiver call; a call on a navigation expression is a call with its receiver classified; a call on `.name` (implicit member) is a call with unknown receiver; prefix operators (`!f()`, `-f()`) are unwrapped to their operand first. A stored property (no computed body) or enum case declared directly in a type's body adds the type names it holds to contains[type]. `T.self` (a navigation expression whose member is `self`) is a 'meta' reference to each type name in its target, carrying the name of the call it is an argument of; any other navigation expression that is not itself a callee is a property read with its receiver. A bare identifier not under a NOT_A_REFERENCE parent and not a callee is an implicit-receiver property read. An assignment whose right side is a closure literal records the target's last identifier in closure_assigns.

branches.effect: its inheritance specifiers added to conforms[name]

units.does: Builds the whole graph from scratch: the unit table, every record's recorded calls, swift_file for every Swift file in the inventory, each file's references resolved by one Resolver, its protocol-requirement and same-stored-format edges and the build wiring, assembled into {'edges': {src: {dst: kind}}, 'units': ..., 'why': {(src, dst): reasons}}. The commands read the same graph from index.py; index.py --verify compares the two.
{node: inventory entry plus its file} for every unit, and a `path::` node of kind 'file' (name the path, lines 1 to the file's length) for every file.

The graph from (src, dst, kind, reason) contributions in any order: a contribution from or to a node not in `units`, or from a node to itself, is dropped; an edge takes the strongest kind any contribution gives it (RANK: certain, then implicit, then possible); a certain or implicit contribution adds its reason to the edge's sorted reasons.

branches.cond: src or dst unknown, or src == dst
stronger than the edge's kind so far

Merges every Swift file's parameter lists, conformances, closure assignments and held types, indexes units by name (Swift units and C/Objective-C functions) and Swift units by their short type name, and takes the repository's types: every unit's short type name and every type that declares a conformance.
A type's short name with every ancestor and protocol it conforms to, transitively.
Whether a unit is a function or initializer with a parameter that has no default value.

The units named `name` that a reference of `kind` can mean: a call matches functions whose labels bind (_labels_match) and properties; a property reference matches properties and functions; optionally only global ones, or only those whose short type is in `types`.
Whether a unit is a type's init(from:) or encode(to:), the members Codable calls.
The units of a type (by short name) whose name is in WITNESS, other than its Codable members.
A type's short name and every repository type its stored values hold, transitively (types outside the repository are not followed).
An implicit edge, reason 'same stored format', from every type's init(from:) to its encode(to:): the decoder reads what the encoder wrote.
(src, dst, kind, reason) for every reference of every unit of one file (resolve).

The edges one unit's references resolve to. A 'meta' reference (`T.self`) to a repository type gives implicit edges, reason 'framework calls', to T's witnesses, and, when the call it is handed to has 'code' in its name (decode, encode, decodeIfPresent), implicit edges, reason 'decodes or encodes T', to the init(from:) and encode(to:) of T and of every type T holds, transitively. A bare call of a repository type name goes to that type's label-matching initializers (certain if one, reason 'initializer') and gives implicit edges, reason 'framework calls', to its witnesses. A reference on self, super or an implicit receiver resolves within the unit's own type family ('own type'); an implicit one with no match falls back to same-file units ('same file'), then global functions ('global function'). A receiver typed by a repository type resolves within that type's family ('typed receiver'); any other receiver against every unit of that name ('unique name'). One candidate gives a certain edge unless the receiver was unresolved and the name is COMMON; then filters drop candidates the reference cannot mean (a property read on an unresolved receiver drops functions that need arguments; app code drops test-target units). An implicit property reference with no candidate is ignored; a call with none whose name is an assigned stored closure gives possible edges to the assigning units ('stored closure').
